title: Highest temperature in London on August 12?
description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 12 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: High pressure across northwest Europe is steering warm continental air into southern England, supporting clear skies and strong daytime heating for London on August 12. Official Met Office guidance currently projects a maximum of 33 °C under largely sunny conditions, while ensemble guidance and shorter-range models cluster between 30–32 °C, reflecting modest uncertainty in boundary-layer mixing and exact wind direction. This setup follows several days of above-average warmth, including a 32 °C peak on August 9, which has reinforced trader confidence in the upper end of the typical August range. With resolution based on the highest official observation from approved London stations, the market-implied odds favor 31–32 °C as the most probable outcomes given the current forecast consensus and limited potential for significant cooling or convective cloud.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader sentiment for Chicago's August 12 high centers on uncertainty around the normal 83°F benchmark amid a developing stormy pattern. Recent NWS guidance highlights increasing thunderstorm chances from Sunday into mid-week, which could enhance cloud cover, boost boundary-layer moisture, and limit insolation enough to cap the high near 80–82°F or allow brief clearing for a push into the mid-80s. Lake Michigan's moderating influence via lake breeze or onshore flow further narrows the range, while model spread in convective timing and intensity creates the tight clustering among 80–81°F, 82–83°F, and 84–85°F bins. Historical August variability and the proximity of resolution amplify sensitivity to the next 12–24 hours of guidance updates.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 12 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/zhengzhou/ZHCC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent rain, extensive cloud cover, and moderating northeasterly winds are keeping model consensus for Zhengzhou’s August 12 maximum near 24–25 °C.** Official extended forecasts from timeanddate and BBC show overcast skies with flash-flood risks and daytime highs of 24 °C, while nearby agency guidance lists a 24 °C ceiling under continued precipitation. These conditions sharply reduce incoming solar radiation and enhance evaporative cooling, pulling temperatures well below the month’s typical 30–33 °C average. The near-even split between 24 °C and 25 °C market shares reflects minor model differences in rainfall timing and boundary-layer moisture that could shift the daily peak by 1 °C. Fresh runs from the China Meteorological Administration and updated satellite observations over the next 24 hours remain the key catalysts for any last-minute adjustment in trader positioning.
